slides.title: Binary addition
slides.main: Binary addition is the same column method, but the carry comes already at 1 + 1.

captions: Lowest position: 1 + 1 = 10, write 0 and carry the one onward
Next position: 0 + 1 + 1 carry = 10, again 0 and a carry
So the carry runs along the positions: 1 + 0 + 1 = 10

slides.title: Half adder
slides.main: Sum is XOR, carry is AND: two gates add two bits.

captions: The sum is exclusive OR: one when the inputs differ
One plus one gives zero and a carry into the next position
One XOR and one AND: A + B = (carry, sum). No input for a carry from below

frames.text:
sum = A xor B
carry = A · B

slides.title: Full adder
slides.sub: Two half adders and an OR
slides.main: The full adder takes three bits: A, B and the carry from the lower position.

captions: The first half adder adds A and B, the second adds the incoming carry, the OR merges the carries
Three ones give 11: sum 1 and carry 1
Sum is XOR of three inputs, carry is one when at least two inputs are ones

frames.text: sum = A xor B xor Cin
= two half adders and an OR gate

slides.title: Ripple-carry adder
slides.main: The carry runs along the chain, and the delay grows with the number of bits.

captions: Three plus two: the lowest gives 1 and a zero carry (1 + 0)
Middle: 1 + 1 = 10, zero and a carry of one into the highest
Highest gets the carry: 0 + 0 + 1 = 1. Result 101 is five
The carry runs along the chain, so the delay grows with the number of bits

slides.title: Increment
slides.main: The lowest bit is inverted, the next is XORed with it: counters need no more.

captions: The lowest bit is always inverted: Y0 = not A0
The high bit toggles only if the low bit was one: Y1 = A1 xor A0
00 → 01 → 10 → 11 → 00: after three comes zero, the carry is lost

slides.title: Adder-subtractor
slides.main: One circuit adds and subtracts: the Sub signal inverts B and adds one.

captions: Sub is zero: XOR passes B as is, the carry into the lowest position is zero
Sub is one: B is inverted, and the carry into the lowest position is one
Minus B is not B plus one: subtraction is reduced to addition

slides.title: Carry and overflow
slides.main: Carry is for unsigned, overflow is for signed numbers.

captions: 15 + 1 in four bits gives 0 and carry C = 1: for unsigned this signals out of range
7 + 1 gives 1000, that is −8: no carry, but the sign of the result is wrong, overflow V = 1
3 + 1 = 4: neither carry nor overflow

slides.title: Subtractors and borrow
slides.main: Direct subtraction helps understand borrowing; in practice we subtract via an adder.

captions: You cannot subtract one from zero without borrowing: we borrow from the higher position
Difference is XOR, borrow is one when subtracting one from zero: not A · B
The full subtractor also takes the borrow from the previous position; usually we subtract via an adder

frames.text:
d = A xor B
b = not A · B
difference = A xor B xor Bin
borrow = not A · B + not (A xor B) · Bin
in practice: A − B = A + not B + 1

slides.title: Comparators
slides.main: Compare the high bits, and only if equal, the low ones.

captions: A > B when A = 1 and B = 0: an AND gate with inverted B
Equality is XNOR: one when the bits are the same
First compare the high bits, and only if they are equal, the low ones

frames.text:
so A > B,
ignore the low bits

slides.title: Carry lookahead
slides.main: Generate and propagate give all the carries in parallel.

captions: In a chain the carry must pass through all positions in turn
For each position we compute: does it generate a carry (G = A·B) and does it pass one along (P = A or B)
All carries are obtained in parallel in two gate levels: faster, but the circuit is larger
